_note: Teardown/breakdown data for the Showroom's exploded view. This GLB is PALETTE-MERGED — its whole exterior is one mesh (PaletteMaterial001) and the interior another (PaletteMaterial002), so wheels/brakes/lights/engine can't be isolated. Degraded teardown: real body + interior meshes lift out, a procedural suspension stand-in spreads, and the rest are honest info-callouts (id NOT engine/drivetrain/suspension so no wrong geometry renders). Anchors in FITTED car space (~3.4 units long, +X nose, +Y up, +Z left). Copy grounded on data/cars/13-mazda-mx-5-miata.json; anchors from frontend/scripts/model_meshes.mjs.

parts.label: Featherweight Roadster Body
parts.summary: A ~2,345 lb steel unibody roadster — the lightness that is the whole point of the car.
parts.detail: Featherweight steel unibody roadster (soft-top ~2,345 lbs; RF retractable fastback ~2,450). Aluminum hood and trunk trim weight to keep the ND near the original's lightweight ethos.
parts.watch: Rock chips and soft-top window/seal wear with age; rust is the enemy on older Miatas, far less so on the galvanized ND.

parts.label: Interior & Driver's Cockpit
parts.summary: A driver-snug two-seat cockpit — the short, notchy shifter falls right to hand.
parts.detail: A tight, driver-focused two-seat cabin built around the short-throw shifter and a low seating position — minimal mass, maximum connection.
parts.watch: Soft-top and window seals wear with age; keep the interior dry to avoid musty tops.

parts.label: 2.0L Skyactiv-G Engine
parts.summary: A free-revving 2.0-liter naturally aspirated four — 181 hp and nearly unbreakable.
parts.detail: 2.0L Skyactiv-G naturally aspirated four — 181 hp at 7,000 rpm in the ND2 (155 hp in the 2016–2018 ND1). Mounted longitudinally, free-revving, and famously durable. (Info callout — this merged model has no separate engine mesh.)
parts.watch: Genuinely durable; just keep up with oil changes and it lasts.

parts.label: 6-Speed Manual & LSD (RWD)
parts.summary: A slick short-throw six-speed sending drive rearward through a limited-slip diff.
parts.detail: A slick 6-speed manual (the one to have) or a 6-speed automatic, driving the rear wheels through a limited-slip differential on Club and GT trims. (Info callout — not a separate mesh in this model.)
parts.watch: Very reliable — the short, notchy shifter is the whole point.

parts.label: Double-Wishbone / Multilink
parts.summary: Double-wishbone front and multilink rear — light, tossable, the entire reason the car exists.
parts.detail: Double-wishbone front and multilink rear — light, tossable, and the whole point of the Miata. (Shown as a procedural stand-in — not a separate mesh in this model.)
parts.watch: Refresh bushings and dampers on high-mile cars to keep the sharpness; coilovers and sway bars are the classic first mod.

parts.label: Wheels & Tires
parts.summary: 16–17" alloys on modest, communicative rubber — grip tuned for feel, not just numbers.
parts.detail: Factory 16-inch (Sport) or 17-inch (Club/GT) alloys on relatively narrow tires — the Miata leans on balance and feel over outright grip. (Info callout — the wheels aren't a separable mesh in this model.)
parts.watch: Lightweight wheels and sticky 200-treadwear tires are the classic first upgrade.

parts.label: Four-Wheel Disc Brakes
parts.summary: Vented front and solid rear discs — more than enough for a ~2,350 lb car.
parts.detail: Vented front and solid rear discs — plenty of stopping power for such a light car. (Info callout — not a separable mesh in this model.)
parts.watch: Pads and fluid are the only upgrade needed for track days.

parts.label: Lighting & Electronics
parts.summary: LED lighting and Mazda's MZD Connect infotainment.
parts.detail: LED head and tail lamps plus Mazda's MZD Connect infotainment with a rotary controller. (Info callout — not a separable mesh in this model.)
parts.watch: Straightforward and reliable; keep the infotainment software current.
